body: Flag: CLEAN. Wipro (promoter group ~72-73%, much of it held for the Azim Premji Foundation's endowment) has a long record of repeated buybacks (2016-2023; the 2023 one ~Rs 12,000 cr -- figures single-source from memory, verify) and dividends, no promoter pledging and no SEBI findings against promoters. The high promoter holding means tender-offer buybacks largely return cash to the promoter/foundation, and Wipro has occasionally been near the 75% MPS ceiling -- a structural, not ethical, issue. Allegations dismissed: an NGO ('India Awake for Transparency') filed multiple complaints alleging Premji transferred assets of three group companies improperly; the Karnataka High Court dismissed a petition under the RBI Act as 'abuse of process' (18-Jan-2021), quashed two private complaints against Premji and his wife, imposed Rs 10 lakh costs for repetitive petitions (Feb-2021), and later convicted two NGO representatives of contempt -- a case where allegations against a promoter failed. Capital-allocation debates: Capco acquisition (2021, $1.45bn) and long underperformance vs. TCS/Infosys; CEO turnover. Premji's philanthropy (pledged equity worth ~$21bn to the foundation, 2019) separated economic interest from the family. Status Nov-2026: Rishad Premji chairman; no open governance issues found.

data.allegations: NGO complaints quashed by Karnataka HC

title: Wipro / Azim Premji — governance history
